No, HD Supply does not sell or distribute advanced consumer or clinical wearable medical devices (such as smart ECG monitors, continuous glucose monitors, or biometric tracking rings). Their healthcare catalog focuses instead on facility maintenance, basic patient care supplies, mobility aids, and resident monitoring systems (like wander management and fall prevention sensors) for institutional and senior living facilities.

- **Founding Year:** 1974 (originally established as Maintenance Warehouse in San Diego, California)

- **Headquarters:** Atlanta, Georgia, United States

- **What the Company Does:** HD Supply is a major industrial distributor of maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) products, janitorial supplies, and operating supplies. It operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of The Home Depot, providing wholesale goods and delivery services to multifamily housing, hospitality, healthcare facilities, and educational institutions. [](https://www.linkedin.com/company/hd-supply)

Common Health Monitoring Devices
Continuous Glucose Monitors (CGMs):
Devices like Dexcom or Freestyle Libre use a tiny sensor under the skin to track sugar levels in real time.
Smartwatches & Wearable ECG:
Brands like Apple, Samsung, and Fitbit offer wrist-based heart rate and electrical heart signal (ECG) tracing.
Sleep Trackers:
Dedicated rings (like Oura) or bedside monitors track sleep stages and recovery metrics.
Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM):
Clinical setups use cellular-enabled blood pressure cuffs, pulse oximeters, and weight scales to send data back to doctors.
